answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock 100 tokens in a vault for 30 days, with one active bid per deposit. Calling two agents marble and jade gives their owner two bids only if both deposits are funded. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. The rule does not prove identities are unique; it makes extra bidding power consume scarce capital, imposing financing costs on the attacker.
